title: Competitor archetypes + provisioning-trigger lab for model fallback readiness
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Why: Enterprise customers with strict SLOs need predictable fallback behavior when primary models become unavailable or economically infeasible. We lack an actionable mapping from competitor model archetypes (size, quantization, latency profile, cost envelope) to provisioning triggers (when to shift to Dedicated, quantized variants, or alternate regions) that PMs, SREs, and Sales can use in playbooks.

What: Run a cross-functional lab to (1) define competitive archetypes for commonly referenced open/hosted models, (2) synthesize provisioning-trigger heuristics (latency, token-cost, availability, tail-error rates) that map to operational actions, and (3) produce a templated decision canvas + test harness that can be used to simulate customer impact for fallback scenarios.

Outcomes: A reproducible lab report, a decision canvas with actionable thresholds, a small synthetic workload harness and dashboard prototype, and a set of recommendations for Console SLO knobs and Optimize rules to automate fallback choices.
acceptance_criteria: A taxonomy of 6-8 competitor archetypes (names, technical profile, typical cost/latency ranges) documented in Confluence
A provisioning-trigger matrix mapping measured signals to actions (canary model, quantized variant, dedicated pool, region failover) with recommended thresholds
A small synthetic workload harness (scripts + configs) that can replay representative traffic and produce metrics used by the matrix
A dashboard prototype (Grafana/Console mock) that visualizes the triggers and a one-page lab report with measured customer impact simulations
Stakeholder reviews completed with SRE, Sales Solutions, and Runtime team and follow-up PRDs for any infra changes
